Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

weft 0.1.0

First release.

Values in prose

  • Inline R with an attribute block prints a computed value through a formatter class: numbers, percentages, p-values, scientific notation, dates, spelled and ordinal counts, lists, ranges and pairs, with keys for decimals, significant figures and list joins. .plus signs a difference; .p takes digits and label.
  • Every class has a function form (fmt_num(), fmt_pct(), fmt_p() and the rest), and weft_str() resolves weft markup in a string from R code.
  • Quantities with units (u()), printed by symbol or name and converted on request.
  • Project settings in _weft.yml for the house style, and project formatters for rules no class covers.

Wording and claims

  • Spans whose wording depends on a value: counts (n), lists (list), conditions and guards (if), and direction (sign), with agreement through ids and back-references.
  • claim() checks a value where it is used and fails the render with the sentence quoted. level = "warn" lists a check without failing. chunk_claims: collect collects failures in chunk code and fails the render at the end.
  • Phrase functions: of_n(), about(), ci() (with short, percentage and signed forms), pm(), clamp(), lookup(), brk() and in_range().
  • arms() lists every wording a document can produce; rehearse() knits it under several sets of parameters.

The dictionary

  • dict.yml holds a project’s chosen values (numbers, quantities, ranges, years, dates, strings, label maps and breaks), each with a definition and an optional decision pointer that verify() resolves. Decision pointers also go on literals, cite spans and claims.
  • A glossary, a Vale rule for spellings to avoid, and dict_seed() to find values that belong in the dictionary.
  • tar_dict() and tar_dict_deps() for targets pipelines.

Other languages and named values

  • Python and Julia values reach prose in knitr documents through py$ and jl_value(), read exactly or refused.
  • Named values: `depth`{.num} in a document on any engine, published from R (weft_put(), weft_values_write()), Python (put(), auto()) or Julia (@put) and resolved by a Pandoc filter. A name can be used above the code that publishes it when it takes one value.

Checking a project

  • lints() reads documents without running them and reports typed numbers, construct errors, cross-reference and citation problems and more.
  • Each render checks its output for unresolved references, values printed as missing and leftover markup, in every format.
  • Each render writes a ledger of the values, wording and tables it printed, and a log of the conditions it raised; changes() compares them with a commit.
  • A commit gate refuses new typed numbers and construct errors, and asks for a trailer when computed values are removed. checks() lists the checks of a project by the value they check.
  • verify() runs the lints, resolves decision pointers, renders every document and checks that no ledger is stale.

Setting up

  • use_weft() sets a project up in one call: activation, Quarto extension and scripts, dictionary, commit hook, GitHub Actions workflow and instructions for coding agents. status() reports what is in place.
